question:
A postmenopausal 87-year-old female presents with a two-day history of blood in her urine. Her family
history is significant for colorectal cancer in her father (age 49) and grandfather (died in his 60s), as
well as ovarian cancer in one sister and endometrial cancer in another sister. Laboratory findings show
normal complete blood count, coagulation studies, and kidney function. Urinalysis reveals more than
100 red blood cells per high-power field (normal: 0-2), with no casts or dysmorphic red cells present.
Which initial diagnostic test would be most appropriate? Answer Choices: (A) Lynch syndrome genetic
testing (B) CT colonography (C) Intravenous pyelogram (IVP) (D) Transvaginal ultrasonography (E)
Cystoscopy (F) Renal ultrasonography (G) CT urography (H) Nuclear medicine renal scan (I) MRI of
the pelvis with contrast (J) Urine cytology and culture
 A. Renal ultrasonography

B. MRI of the pelvis with contrast
C. Urine cytology and culture
D. CT urography
E. Transvaginal ultrasonography
F. Intravenous pyelogram (IVP)
G. CT colonography
H. Nuclear medicine renal scan
I. Lynch syndrome genetic testing
J. Cystoscopy
